### The Speck and the Log
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-september-26-2024.html
Passage: Luke 6:42
Points:
- Jesus uses the contrast between a speck and a structural beam to command self-examination first.
- Fallen human nature is quick to obsess over other people's sins while ignoring personal guilt.
- Pointing out another person's faults without dealing with one's own sin amounts to hypocrisy.
- Genuine help requires approaching others from a place of humble love rather than presumptuous superiority.

### Fault Finders
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/fault-finders-greg-laurie-daily-devotion-may-14.html
Passage: Matthew 7:3
Points:
- People frequently project their own hidden sins and selfish motives onto other people.
- Jesus warns against obsessing over small specks in others while ignoring a large plank in oneself.
- While Christians can assess external actions, they cannot see or judge the human heart.
- Believers must focus on maintaining personal character and integrity rather than condemning others.
